xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5586: Add Gemini 4 Carbon, Neon and Hydrogen; update Google tier mapping and deprecation remaps

plan.title: Add Gemini 4 Carbon, Neon and Hydrogen; update Google tier mapping and deprecation remaps
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: One Google catalog refresh: 26 files, 15 of them tests or docs, all edits additive rows in the model registry. The surface counter treats each doc file as its own subsystem (docs/USAGE.md, docs/MODEL-CONTEXT-AUDIT.md, changelog.d/pan-5586.md), which pushes the subsystem count to 7. Splitting into sibling issues would ship ids that are selectable but unpriced or tier ids pi cannot bind.

narratives.Problem: Google released gemini-4-carbon, gemini-4-neon and gemini-4-hydrogen in November 2026. Overdeck does not know them: users cannot pick them, cost tracking cannot price them, pi launches on pi 0.85/1.5.2 cannot bind them, and PROVIDERS.google.tierModels still names the Gemini 3.1 generation. MODEL_DEPRECATIONS also remaps gemini-2.5-pro/flash to ids Google no longer routes them to.
narratives.Proposal: Follow the gemini-4-argon registration pattern (PRD .pan/drafts/PAN-5586.md): capability rows and classes, provider routing and selectable lists, cost rows, pi/omp provisioning, dashboard picker and friendly names, then set Google tierModels to neon/carbon/hydrogen and remap gemini-2.5-pro -> gemini-3.8-flash and gemini-2.5-flash -> gemini-3.5-flash-lite in both MODEL_DEPRECATIONS and MODEL_API_IDS. Comment on PAN-4555 so its 2026-12-01 price raise also covers Carbon. Document the change in docs/USAGE.md, docs/MODEL-CONTEXT-AUDIT.md and changelog.d/pan-5586.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No change to gemini-4-argon's prices, capability row or supportsImages flag (PAN-4555 owns the Argon raise).
- No dated-pricing mechanism in cost.ts; Carbon is priced exactly like Argon on the branch.
- No ohmypi behavior changes beyond adding three registry rows (omp removal is PAN-4003).
- No edits to history: .pan/, .release/ and changelog.mdx keep their existing Argon text.
- No retirement of gemini-3.1-pro-preview, gemini-3-flash-preview or any other live Google id.
- No new FALLBACK_MAP rows for gemini-3.8-flash or gemini-3.5-flash-lite (pre-existing gap).
- No growth of src/dashboard/server/routes/settings.ts and no edit to src/lib/model-capabilities.ts; no allowlist raise.
- No new frontend test file and no edit to scripts/frontend-test-subset.txt.

autoDecisions.summary: Insert the three ids directly after gemini-4-argon in every ordered list, in the order neon, carbon, hydrogen.
autoDecisions.rationale: Argon stays first, so the existing settings-model-catalog assertion existing.google[0] === Argon keeps holding and the diff stays minimal.

autoDecisions.summary: Google tierModels follow the issue: opus gemini-4-neon, sonnet gemini-4-carbon, haiku gemini-4-hydrogen.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue is explicit and Google publishes no tier labels, although its index calls Carbon 'our strongest reasoning model'; Neon is the most expensive Gemini 4 model through 2026-11-30.

autoDecisions.summary: Capability classes: neon frontier, carbon frontier, hydrogen workhorse.
autoDecisions.rationale: Carbon costs what Argon (frontier) costs and Google calls it its strongest reasoning model; Hydrogen costs more than gemini-3.6-flash (workhorse), so 'small' would make tier-fitness warn on every medium tier using Google's haiku id. The class only drives Settings warnings.

autoDecisions.summary: Carbon uses Argon's introductory rates ($2/$10/$0.10, blended 6) unless PAN-4555 already merged, in which case it uses list rates ($4/$20/$0.20, blended 12).
autoDecisions.rationale: No dated-pricing mechanism exists on main; PAN-4555 is a manual date-gated edit, so Carbon must move in lockstep with Argon. A comment on PAN-4555 adds Carbon to that edit.

autoDecisions.summary: Align MODEL_API_IDS (Settings test route) with the new gemini-2.5 remaps.
autoDecisions.rationale: Google routes 2.5 Pro to 3.8 Flash and 2.5 Flash to 3.5 Flash-Lite from 2026-12-01; probing a different wire model than Google serves would mislead the key test.

autoDecisions.summary: Hydrogen gets xhigh thinking even though the issue lists xhigh only for Neon.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue says the official page wins; Google's thinking guide and pi 1.6.0's catalog both list xhigh for Hydrogen. The PR body must note the difference.

autoDecisions.summary: Skill scores inherit: Neon and Carbon copy Argon's skills, Hydrogen copies gemini-3.8-flash's; all three set supportsImages true and supportsSamplingParams false.
autoDecisions.rationale: The repo convention is to inherit the previous family baseline until benchmarked; Google lists image input and states sampling parameters are ignored on all three.

autoDecisions.summary: Friendly-name assertions go in gemini-qwen-glm-catalog.test.ts, not dashboard-utils.test.ts.
autoDecisions.rationale: Only the former is in scripts/frontend-test-subset.txt, so CI runs it; no new frontend test file is needed.

metadata.acJustification: One indivisible commit: growing the GoogleModel union forces rows in MODEL_CAPABILITIES and MODEL_PROVIDERS (Record<ModelId,...>), and the rows immediately change picker and fallback test counts.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-1. Add 'gemini-4-neon' | 'gemini-4-carbon' | 'gemini-4-hydrogen' after 'gemini-4-argon' in the GoogleModel union (src/lib/settings.ts line 42). In src/lib/model-capability-additions.ts insert three rows right after the gemini-4-argon row (ends line 176), in the order neon, carbon, hydrogen, with the exact fields and notes strings in the PRD: contextWindow 1048576, maxOutputTokens 65536, supportsImages true, supportsSamplingParams false; costPer1MTokens 9 / 6 / 4.5; effortLevels neon and hydrogen ['low','medium','high','xhigh'], carbon ['low','medium','high']; skills copied from gemini-4-argon (neon, carbon) and gemini-3.8-flash (hydrogen). In src/lib/model-capability-class.ts add neon and carbon as 'frontier' after the Argon row (line 33) and hydrogen as 'workhorse' after gemini-3.6-flash (line 70). In src/lib/model-fallback.ts add the three ids to MODEL_PROVIDERS as 'google' (after line 74) and to FALLBACK_MAP after the Argon row (line 203): neon and carbon -> 'claude-sonnet-5-5', hydrogen -> 'claude-haiku-4-5'. Update tests exactly as PRD WI-1 step 5 lists (model-capabilities it.each, settings-model-catalog filter + first-four-ids assertion, model-fallback counts 11->14 (line 166), 20->23 (line 441, comment '13 Anthropic + 10 current Google') and 46->49 (line 405, comment '13 Anthropic + 15 OpenAI + 10 Google + 11 Kimi') plus provider and fallback expectations). If PAN-4555 already merged on the branch (Argon cost row reads inputPer1k 0.004), Carbon's costPer1MTokens is 12 instead of 6.
